title: Farming in Goa
heading: Start or sustain farming in Goa
summary: Land checks, Krishi Card registration, soil advice, schemes and damage records.
markdown:
**Draft reviewed against collected sources on 22 October 2026. Legal and service verification remains open.**

Start with the right to use the land, then register the farming activity, get advice for the site and check support before spending. A Krishi Card, a subsidy sanction and a permission to change land use serve different purposes. This guide helps individual growers and community groups organise those steps; it does not certify a land transaction or a scheme entitlement.

## Choose your first step

| Your situation | Start here |
| --- | --- |
| You want to buy, lease or use somebody else's land | Assemble the land records and obtain advice on title, tenancy, transfer restrictions and authority to cultivate. |
| You already cultivate and need registration or support | Approach the Zonal Agriculture Office for the location of the holding, using the [registration enquiry](/guides/templates/09-farming-registration-enquiry.txt). |
| You need crop, soil or pest advice | Contact the relevant Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK), Agriculture office or ICAR-CCARI with your crop and site details. |
| A bund has failed, salt water has entered, or crops are damaged | Record the damage promptly and ask the Agriculture office for inspection and the relevant reporting or claim route. |
| You plan a shed, well, pond, filling or tree removal | Check the separate permissions before commissioning work. Use the [building guide](/read/guide-building) and [environmental protection guide](/read/guide-environmental-protection). |

The Directorate's charter lists Zonal Agriculture Offices, soil laboratories, training and subject officers on physical pages 42–43. ICAR-CCARI describes access to crop advice, planting material and publications through its dissemination centre. [Agriculture charter][FR1]; [ICAR services][FR8]

**Verification needed AG01:** confirm the office serving the particular village, opening hours, appointment requirements and current submission route. Published staff lists are not proof of an available appointment.

## 1. Establish the land and your authority to cultivate

Create a parcel file containing the village, taluka, survey and subdivision numbers, area, current Form I and XIV, survey plan, access details and the documents explaining your interest in the land. Include relevant sale, succession, lease, consent or authority documents. Record any co-owner, tenant, comunidade or other interest requiring examination. Keep conflicting names or areas visible for resolution.

Before signing a transaction, ask a Goa land-law practitioner to check title and existing rights, the validity of the proposed arrangement, and whether permission is required. The Agricultural Tenancy Act is a separate legal framework; an informal consent letter or a registration application does not settle tenancy rights. [Tenancy Act][FR3]

The **2023 agricultural-transfer Act uses a specific definition tied to paddy cultivation**, with an exclusion for land earmarked for other uses in a TCP plan. Its section 3 restricts transfers of land within that definition and provides a Collector-permission mechanism in specified circumstances. Do not apply a blanket “anyone can buy farmland” or “no newcomer can farm” rule. [2023 Act, sections 2–4][FR2]

**Verification needed AG02:** check commencement, current rules and amendments, the actual parcel's legal classification, the proposed transaction, and any necessary Collector or Mamlatdar process. The original Act alone is not a complete transaction checklist. For inherited or tenanted holdings, obtain case-specific advice before promising a sale, lease or change of use.

Write down a simple proposed activity: crops, cultivated area, water source, intended structures, earthworks and whether any produce will be processed or sold through a new business. This makes separate permission questions easier to answer.

## 2. Apply for or update the Krishi Card

Ask the Zonal Agriculture Office for the current form and checklist for your applicant type. The collected charter distinguishes an individual farmer from an institution, NGO, self-help group or company. Its checklist includes land records, the applicable document supporting use of the holding, identity and bank information, a mandate and soil samples. Group applications also need registration and authority documents. [Charter, physical page 2][FR1]

Official starting forms are available for an [individual farmer][FR4] and a [farmers group][FR5]. Take these as starting documents and confirm that the receiving office still accepts them.

1. List all holdings accurately, using the same identifiers as the supporting records.
2. Ask how to handle joint, inherited, leased or disputed records before signing a declaration.
3. Ask which originals must be shown and which copies are retained. Share identity and bank documents only through the confirmed official channel.
4. Obtain the prescribed bank mandate and sampling instructions.
5. Submit the accepted application, retain a full copy and obtain a dated receipt or reference.
6. Check the issued card or record for correct names, holdings and bank details; request corrections in writing.

**Verification needed AG03:** confirm the accepted form version, fees if any, nominee requirements, identity alternatives where applicable, sampling arrangements and processing time. Do not present this checklist as a fixed legal requirement for every applicant category.

A June 2025 Agriculture notice asks farmers to update Aadhaar-seeded bank details through the Zonal office and warns that a later bank-seeding change can change the account receiving benefits. Ask both the bank and the office to confirm the relevant account and mapping. Do not disclose an OTP or banking password to a helper. [Official bank-update notice][FR6]

## 3. Get a soil and crop plan before buying inputs

Ask the laboratory or extension officer how to collect and label samples for each distinct field or management area, what quantity is needed, what tests they offer, and whether water testing is appropriate. Avoid mixing visibly different soils into one sample without their advice. Keep the sample reference linked to the survey number and field sketch.

ICAR's laboratory directory lists testing at KVK North Goa in Ela, the Agriculture Farmers Training Centre in Ela, and KVK South Goa in Margao. Use the directory to choose an enquiry route; verify current reception, charges and turnaround. [Laboratory directory][FR7]

Bring the crop history, irrigation source, flooding or salinity observations, photographs and soil report to the advisory visit. Ask for a locally suitable crop or variety, season, water plan, nutrient recommendation, pest-monitoring method and harvest plan. ICAR-CCARI publishes recommended practices for Goa crops and offers technology advice. [ICAR services][FR8]

Use the [farm planning and activity log](/guides/templates/10-farm-plan-and-log.md). Record why an input was recommended, the product and batch, date, quantity and area treated. Request crop-specific advice before using pesticides; follow the approved label and applicable restrictions. The charter treats seed, fertilizer, insecticide and nursery businesses as separate licensing subjects, so growing crops does not automatically authorise selling regulated inputs. [Charter, physical pages 33–41][FR1]

**Verification needed AG04:** confirm the current crop recommendation, authorised input and use, any harvest interval, and laboratory service details with the appropriate specialist. No pesticide dose, fertilizer rate or yield promise is supplied here. An “organic” marketing or certification claim needs its own applicable standards check.

## 4. Ask about support before committing money

Use the [scheme and damage enquiry](/guides/templates/11-farming-support-or-damage.txt) to request the current notification for the particular activity. The charter describes support across crops, irrigation, machinery, community farming, organic inputs and khazan protection. Treat those headings as questions to ask, not a guarantee that a budget or application window is open. [Agriculture charter][FR1]

For each possible scheme, obtain written answers to:

- Who can apply, and which holding, crop, area or group conditions apply?
- Is prior approval or an inspection needed before purchase or work starts?
- What is the application deadline, eligible cost, contribution, ceiling and funding availability?
- Are particular suppliers, specifications, invoices, payment methods or photographs required?
- Can the same expense receive another subsidy? What must be disclosed?
- What triggers payment, what evidence closes the claim, and how can a rejection be reviewed?

Keep the notification, application, acknowledgement, sanction, invoices and payment record together. A received application is not a sanction. A sanction is not proof of payment. Budget using your confirmed contribution and the actual payment conditions.

**Verification needed AG05:** all amounts, current financial-year terms, eligibility, spending sequence, claim periods and appeal routes need checking against the relevant scheme notification. Older handbook figures have deliberately not been reproduced.

## 5. Treat water, khazan works and farm structures separately

For a proposed well or groundwater extraction, ask the Water Resources Department which registration or permission applies to the location and intended use. Goa has a Ground Water Regulation Act and Rules; an agriculture scheme sanction does not answer that separate question. [WRD legislation index][FR9]

Before cutting a slope or filling low-lying land, obtain advice from TCP about section 17A and any other applicable controls. Before building a shed or changing use, follow the [building guide](/read/guide-building). For tree removal, coastal land, mangroves, forest or a wetland setting, follow the [environmental guide](/read/guide-environmental-protection). [TCP section 17A procedure][FR10]

For khazan land, identify the bund, sluice, responsible association or authority, and affected cultivators. Ask the Agriculture Soil Conservation Division and relevant revenue authority who may authorise the repair and how costs and responsibilities are shared. The charter has a separate khazan-protection section. Do not breach a bund, change a sluice setting or fill a channel on the assumption that a farm needs it. [Charter, physical pages 30–31 and 42][FR1]

**Verification needed AG06:** verify the actual water/land status, tenants' association or other management rights, current repair scheme and overlapping permissions. Obtain a site-specific answer before physical work.

## 6. Record damage and follow a claim through

If safe, photograph damage before clearing it. Note when it began, the crop and stage, affected area, water level or other observations, and any action already taken. Keep purchase, cultivation and harvest records. Distinguish observed damage from an unconfirmed cause.

Notify the Zonal Agriculture Office promptly and ask for an inspection, the relevant disaster-relief, crop-loss or insurance route, and the actual deadline. For an insured crop, notify the insurer through its policy channel as well; a departmental complaint may not satisfy an insurance condition. For wildlife damage, contact the Forest Department for the applicable route and safe response. Do not poison, trap or injure wildlife.

Use the [reporting guide](/read/guide-reporting) for a numbered follow-up or a targeted RTI request for inspection and decision records. Record an office-promised date separately from a statutory or scheme deadline.

**Verification needed AG07:** compensation is not automatic. Check current notified events, eligible crops/areas, evidence requirements, reporting period, assessment authority and interaction with insurance.

## Worked example

A group wants to restart cultivation on a low-lying holding and buy a pump. First, establish who can authorise cultivation and whether tenancy or transfer restrictions affect the arrangement. Then ask the Zonal office about group registration and the current pump scheme, and obtain soil/water advice. Check any well, electricity, bund or earthwork permissions separately. Order equipment only after the scheme's required approval stage is clear. Keep the receipt, inspection and payment evidence in one file.

## Templates and review

- [Registration enquiry](/guides/templates/09-farming-registration-enquiry.txt)
- [Farm plan and log](/guides/templates/10-farm-plan-and-log.md)
- [Support or damage enquiry](/guides/templates/11-farming-support-or-damage.txt)
- [Verification register](/read/guide-verification) and [source register](/read/guide-sources)

These supporting templates do not replace statutory forms, land documents or a sanction. Existing Act for Goa farmer stories and resources remain useful background; current legal and application steps should point to the official sources below.

title: Animal welfare in Goa
heading: Help an animal and report cruelty in Goa
summary: Find veterinary or wildlife help, report cruelty and check current community-animal procedures.
markdown:
**Draft reviewed against collected sources on 22 October 2026. Contact availability and current local implementation still need verification.**

Choose the response by the situation: a person exposed to rabies needs medical care; an injured domestic animal needs veterinary assistance; cruelty may need police action; wildlife needs the Forest Department. An organisation's listing does not establish that it can dispatch a vehicle or accept an animal.

## Start with the immediate need

| Situation | First action |
| --- | --- |
| A person has been bitten, scratched or exposed to potentially infectious saliva | Wash the exposed wound and seek urgent medical assessment. Do not wait for animal rescue or observation. |
| A domestic animal is injured, sick or trapped | Contact the nearest appropriate veterinary service; describe the location, species, condition and access. Confirm who can attend or receive it. |
| You witness violence, suspected poisoning or serious neglect | Request police assistance and veterinary assessment; document facts safely. |
| A snake, wild bird or other wildlife is injured or inside a building | Keep people and pets away and contact Forest Department rescue services. Avoid handling it. |
| Cattle or dogs create an immediate road hazard | Report the precise road and direction to police/road responders and the local body; request humane animal handling. Do not enter traffic to capture them. |
| You need sterilisation, vaccination or help with a community-dog dispute | Contact the local body and jurisdictional veterinary officer; ask which recognised programme and current directions apply. |

The AHVS [cruelty and distress contact page][AN1] links to veterinary, hospital, Panchayat, police, DSPCA and nodal-officer routes. Its [veterinary directory][AN2] lists facilities by location. Use these to choose a relevant service, then confirm availability.

## Human exposure needs medical care now

After a bite or scratch, wash the wound thoroughly with soap and running water for **at least 15 minutes** and seek urgent medical assessment for rabies post-exposure care. Saliva on broken skin or a mucous membrane can also be an exposure. A clinician determines the vaccine and any immunoglobulin or monoclonal-antibody treatment needed; do not wait for symptoms or for a complaint to be registered. [WHO rabies guidance, prevention and post-exposure prophylaxis][AN3]

Tell the clinician when and how the exposure happened and any previous rabies vaccination. Keep the treatment record and follow the schedule provided. Report the animal's location separately to the veterinary/local authority without attempting to capture it yourself. For immediate danger to people, contact police or ambulance services through the official Goa emergency directory. [Goa emergency numbers][AN4]

**Verification needed AW01:** a Goa clinician should check the final medical wording and current treatment-centre referral information. No facility's vaccine stock, immunoglobulin availability or opening hours has been confirmed. The emergency numbers are published channels, not tested dispatches.

## Find the right animal service

### Domestic animals

Use the [AHVS emergency-contact directory][AN2] to locate the veterinary hospital or dispensary serving the area. The state portal also lists office contacts for Tonca, Mapusa, Sonsodo and Curti-Ponda. Use the AHVS head-office contact page for departmental enquiries; its office contacts are not established here as round-the-clock rescue services. [Department directory][AN5]; [AHVS head office][AN6]

Before moving an animal, ask:

- Can you attend this location, or which facility can receive this species now?
- Is a trained handler or suitable vehicle needed, and who will arrange it?
- Are there charges, admission conditions or an owner-consent requirement?
- Who is the responsible contact, and what is the case or referral number?

Use the [animal assistance request and handover record](/guides/templates/12-animal-assistance.txt). Do not give medicines, induce vomiting or attempt a hazardous capture based on this guide. If poisoning is suspected, keep people and other animals away from the suspected material and ask the veterinarian/police how evidence should be preserved.

### Wildlife

The Forest Department contact page lists separate North and South Goa helplines, labelled as available around the clock, and a general office contact. Give the village, map pin, species if known and immediate risk. If you cannot identify the animal, describe it and send a photograph only if safe. [Forest contact page][AN7]

Keep your distance; avoid crowding, feeding, capturing or relocating the animal. Ask the department to arrange or identify an authorised responder. A volunteer contact or social-media post is not a wildlife possession or relocation permission. The official Forest site provides the wildlife-law and protected-area references. [Forest Department][AN8]

**Verification needed AW02:** the source-listed numbers, directory assignments, service boundaries, response times, transport, fees and responder authorisation need direct verification. If one route fails, try the relevant local veterinary office or Forest office and record the referral. Escalate immediate human danger through emergency services.

## Report suspected cruelty with usable evidence

The Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act places a duty on people in charge of animals to take reasonable measures for their wellbeing and to prevent unnecessary pain or suffering. Section 11 addresses specified forms of cruel treatment. Use observed facts, not a guessed legal charge. [PCA Act, sections 3 and 11][AN9]

1. Record the time, exact location, species and number of animals, and what you personally observed. Mark second-hand reports as such.
2. Preserve original photographs or video taken from a lawful, safe position. Record injuries as observations; a veterinarian should diagnose and document them.
3. Where possible, record a vehicle, premises or person identifier accurately. Do not guess identities or publish private details in an appeal for help.
4. Contact the jurisdictional police station for suspected offences, and AHVS for veterinary assistance and the appropriate welfare authority. The official cruelty page includes police, DSPCA and nodal contacts. Wildlife cases should also go to Forest authorities. [AHVS routes][AN1]; [Goa cruelty SOP][AN10]
5. Submit the [cruelty complaint](/guides/templates/13-animal-cruelty-complaint.txt), request acknowledgement and ask what complaint/FIR or other record has been made, as applicable.
6. Ask for veterinary examination and preservation of relevant evidence through the authorities. Do not seize an animal or enter private premises yourself.

The **2020 Goa SOP contains historical criminal-law references**. It supports coordination, but its old offence numbers should not be copied into a current complaint. Police or a lawyer should identify the current provisions and procedure. [Goa SOP][AN10]

**Verification needed AW03:** confirm current criminal-law provisions, cognizability and police procedure for the actual facts, competent local welfare bodies and the latest SOP. This guide does not promise that every allegation must result in the same criminal process, or that a complainant may take custody.

If no action follows, send a dated factual follow-up with the original reference and new evidence. Use the [reporting guide](/read/guide-reporting) and [case log](/guides/templates/05-case-log.md). Obtain legal advice promptly about urgent protection, an adverse decision or a refused criminal complaint; the [Goa legal-aid service][AN11] explains its assistance and eligibility.

## Request community-animal care through the local programme

Ask the Panchayat, municipality or other responsible local authority for the jurisdictional veterinary officer, the programme operator, current project recognition and complaint route. The ABC Rules 2023 provide for project recognition, local-authority responsibilities, veterinary care, records and monitoring. General NGO recognition and recognition for an ABC project are different questions. [ABC Rules, rules 3, 8–14 and schedules][AN12]

Use the [community-animal service enquiry](/guides/templates/14-community-animal-service.txt) to request:

- A vaccination or sterilisation assessment, describing identifiable animals and known medical needs.
- The responsible centre and veterinary supervisor, with the recognised project details.
- Capture, transport, treatment, recovery and individual-record arrangements.
- The lawful destination after treatment, identifying the site category and applicable directions.
- A contact for missed service, injury, unsafe handling or disagreement.

Do not organise an informal capture or move dogs to another locality. If an authorised operation appears harmful, record the specific conduct safely and use the complaint route. A disputed removal decision and alleged cruelty during handling need to be described separately.

## Check current directions before advising on feeding or release

The **Supreme Court judgment of 19 May 2026, 2026 INSC 506**, upholds the institutional-premises directions considered there, including the prohibition on re-release at those locations. It also directs authorities to assess extension to other high-footfall public spaces and places ongoing compliance oversight with High Courts. It does not justify a resident deciding a relocation rule on their own. [Judgment, paragraphs 75–76, 108(D) and 111][AN13]

Consequently, do not publish a universal “release every dog at the same spot” rule or a universal feeding entitlement from an older leaflet. For a school, hospital, transport facility or other disputed place, ask the responsible authority for the applicable order, site designation, nodal officer and humane management arrangements. For a residential feeding dispute, ask for the applicable designated arrangement and dispute process, taking account of the current court directions as well as the rules. [ABC Rules, rule 20][AN12]; [2026 judgment][AN13]

**Verification needed AW04:** retrieve and reconcile the latest Supreme Court, Bombay High Court/Goa orders, AWBI institutional SOP and local implementation decisions before giving site-specific advice. The May judgment is verified source material, not a certification that no later order exists. No operational euthanasia advice is provided; such decisions require the competent veterinary and legal process.

## Keep care and custody records

For a pet or livestock animal in your charge, agree a vaccination, preventive-care and identification plan with a veterinarian. Keep proof of ownership or lawful handover, medical records and emergency contacts. Check local registration requirements, travel rules or business permissions before breeding, sale, boarding or transport. The duty of care applies while an animal is in your custody. [PCA Act, section 3][AN9]

For a rescue handover, record who accepted the animal, where, when, its identifiers and condition, and the agreed next update. Distinguish temporary care from an ownership transfer. Do not promise shelter admission, adoption approval, reimbursement or a right to reclaim without the receiving authority's process.

**Verification needed AW05:** confirm species-specific transport, adoption, livestock, pet-registration and commercial-activity requirements for the actual case. These subjects need separate checklists if Act for Goa expands this guide.

## Worked example and templates

For an injured dog near a school, arrange urgent veterinary help and tell the school/local-body nodal contact where it is. Record any human exposure for medical care. Ask the authority for the applicable institutional process and treatment destination; do not assume the dog will be returned to the school. Record the handover and request a case update. Report any observed cruelty separately with evidence.

- [Assistance and handover](/guides/templates/12-animal-assistance.txt)
- [Cruelty complaint](/guides/templates/13-animal-cruelty-complaint.txt)
- [Community-animal service enquiry](/guides/templates/14-community-animal-service.txt)
- [Verification register](/read/guide-verification) and [source register](/read/guide-sources)

Build on Act for Goa's [animal-rights resource](https://actforgoa.org/resource/animal-rights-in-india/) and [snake-volunteer list](https://actforgoa.org/resource/snake-rescue-volunteers-in-goa/), while checking dates, current law and actual service availability.

title: Environmental protection in Goa
heading: Protect trees, water, coast and biodiversity in Goa
summary: Check tree, coastal and wetland protections, request inspection and take part in decisions.
markdown:
**Draft reviewed against collected sources on 22 October 2026. Site classifications, current orders and submission channels still need verification.**

Begin with the place and the observed activity. A tree-felling permission, building licence, coastal clearance and pollution consent answer different questions. Several protections may apply to the same site. Use this guide to gather the relevant records, request inspection and participate in a decision; a map pin alone cannot establish a breach.

## 1. Record the place and choose the authority

Use the [site and protection checklist](/guides/templates/15-environment-site-check.md). Record village/town, taluka, survey/subdivision number if known, a map pin, landmarks, dates and what you observed. Mark approximate locations and uncertain boundaries explicitly. Photographs from public or otherwise lawful positions can show activity without establishing its legal classification.

| Observed issue | First authority or record-holder to identify |
| --- | --- |
| Tree cutting, suspected forest clearance, wildlife habitat damage | Jurisdictional Forest office/Tree Officer; ask about forest and protected-area status as well as felling permission. |
| Coastal, estuarine, mangrove or dune development | Goa Coastal Zone Management Authority (GCZMA); local planning/body records may also matter. |
| Lake or suspected wetland filling | Goa State Wetland Authority (GSWA), with TCP/local-body referral where land development is involved. |
| Hill cutting or low-lying land filling | TCP for section 17A; other authorities according to forest, coastal, wetland or water impacts. |
| Sewage, discharge, emissions, waste dumping or noise | GSPCB and the relevant local body or utility, according to the source and service responsibility. |
| Blocked channel, water abstraction or well works | Water Resources Department and the relevant local/revenue authority; ask which office controls the watercourse or activity. |
| A proposed project or draft notification | The authority and submission channel named in the actual consultation notice. |

Official starting points are the [Forest Department][EN1], [environment department charter][EN2], [GCZMA][EN3], [TCP procedure][EN4], [GSPCB][EN5] and [WRD legislation index][EN6].

**Verification needed EP01:** confirm the precise jurisdiction, current officer and accepted channel. A local body and a specialist regulator may both have roles; a copy to one is not proof that the other registered the case. Ask each office to identify the part it will address.

For immediate danger to people or a fire, use emergency services. For continuing environmental damage, request urgent inspection and explain what is changing; the urgency label does not itself create a stop-work order.

## 2. Check tree permissions and forest status separately

Goa's Preservation of Trees Act contains restrictions on felling/removal and a permission process, with exceptions and conditions. Begin by asking the Tree Officer whether the actual operation requires permission and whether an order exists. Ownership of the land does not by itself settle that question. [Trees Act, sections 8–10][EN7]

Request the application, site sketch, inspection report, tree inventory, permission/refusal, conditions, validity, extension and any transport permission applicable to the produce. Compare the approved location, species, number and identifiers with what can be observed safely. A photograph or rough tree count is a reason to ask for inspection, not proof that the entire operation is unlawful.

For somebody seeking permission, Goa Online provides **Form B** and an official checklist describes application, verification, inspection and approval stages. Use the prescribed route with the current required ownership/authority documents and site details; confirm payment only through the official process. [Goa Online service][EN8]; [official checklist][EN9]

**Verification needed EP02:** check the current Act/rules, subsequent notifications, species exceptions, emergency-tree procedure, co-owner requirements, felling and transit conditions, fees and appeal rights. The checklist contains overlapping tree-count bands, so this draft does not reproduce its approval thresholds. Do not rely on elapsed time alone as permission or attempt emergency felling using this guide.

If forest status is uncertain, ask Forest authorities for the applicable records and orders, including any private-forest identification, protected-area boundary or eco-sensitive-zone notification. A revenue entry or visible absence of dense trees does not resolve all forest questions. The Forest website publishes separate private-forest and protected-area resources. [Forest Department][EN1]

Act for Goa already has [tree-cutting guidance](https://actforgoa.org/resource/how-to-stop-tree-cutting/) and a [reporting resource](https://actforgoa.org/resource/report-tree-cutting/). Use the evidence approach, while checking every legal citation and contact against current official material.

## 3. Establish the coastal plan and clearance applying to the site

Open the [GCZMA website][EN3] and its [Final CZMP Goa document page][EN10]. Ask for the **approved plan sheet, approval letter, amendments/corrections and applicable CRZ notification** for the exact location. Record the map edition, scale and authority. A page heading, draft sheet or third-party overlay is not proof of the operative boundary.

Request the project's coastal application, authorised demarcation/site plan where applicable, clearance or refusal, conditions and inspection records. Compare the actual activity with the permission's stated purpose and location. Also check the separate planning, local-body and other environmental permissions relevant to the work.

Do not infer one universal distance from the sea or river that makes construction lawful. Category, tidal influence, feature, approved map, dates and the activity all matter. The corpus contains a central CRZ 2019 compilation, but its existence does not establish which approved Goa plan applies to a particular parcel. [Central CRZ compilation][EN11]

**Verification needed EP03:** obtain the current Goa approval package, applicable notification and amendments, corrected site sheet, relevant court orders and qualified interpretation of any contested demarcation. No parcel classification or coastal setback is certified here.

## 4. Distinguish a wetland record from a final notification

Ask GSWA for the site's name and identifier, inventory/brief document, any Ramsar designation or final notification, schedules, boundary and zone-of-influence map, and later amendments or orders. Ask which restrictions and management authority apply.

The Wetlands Rules 2017 distinguish their definition and scope from ordinary descriptions of wet ground. Rule 2 excludes categories including paddy fields and river channels; rule 3 addresses applicability and areas covered by specified other regimes. For wetlands within the rules' scope, rule 4 includes prohibitions such as conversion/encroachment, solid-waste dumping and untreated waste discharge. Site facts and overlapping laws still matter. [Wetlands Rules, rules 2–4][EN12]

**A draft notification is a proposal, not the final notification.** The corpus's March 2023 Goa gazette expressly invites objections and suggestions. Use it to trace the process and obtain the eventual outcome; do not cite it as proof that its proposed schedules became operative. Conversely, absence from one final-notification list does not prove that a place has no protection under another law or court direction. [Goa draft notifications][EN13]; [implementation guidance][EN14]

The GSWA [gazette index][EN15] is a discovery route. Direct retrieval failed during review. If it remains unavailable, ask GSWA or the environment department for the numbered final notification and maps, using the [records and inspection request](/guides/templates/16-environment-records-and-inspection.txt) and, if necessary, the RTI route in the [reporting guide](/read/guide-reporting).

**Verification needed EP04:** verify final versus draft status, amendments, applicable court protection, boundary, zone of influence and the current GSWA contact/submission channel. The national guidance does not determine an individual lake's present status.

## 5. Report pollution, filling or obstruction with specific observations

For suspected pollution, record the location and apparent source, date/time, duration, visible discharge, odour, affected water or land, and any recurring pattern. Request official inspection or sampling. Avoid claiming a chemical identity or statutory measurement from a photograph, smell or phone application.

GSPCB publishes **mail.gspcb@gov.in** for complaints/grievances. Save the sent message and attachments and ask for a reference. Its online complaint page requires a usable browser session. Use the local body for a collection/drainage service issue and GSPCB for the pollution concern as appropriate. [GSPCB][EN5]

For hill cutting or low-lying filling, identify both the excavation/fill location and any affected drain, stream or neighbouring land. TCP publishes a separate section 17A permission process. Ask for that permission and its approved plan/conditions without assuming it replaces other required approvals. [TCP section 17A][EN4]

For a blocked watercourse or abstraction, ask WRD to identify the competent office, relevant record and inspection route. Do not excavate a new channel, collect hazardous samples or enter flowing/flooded water to prove a case. [WRD legal framework][EN6]

**Verification needed EP05:** confirm live complaint handling, the applicable consent or authorisation, current pollution/waste requirements and the inspection/sampling authority. No universal response period or automatic enforcement outcome is claimed.

## 6. Make a useful consultation submission

GSPCB publishes project-specific public-hearing notices. A hearing is part of the decision process where required; it is not itself the final environmental clearance. Start from the actual notice and project identity. [Official public-hearing example][EN16]

1. Save the notice and record the project/proponent, survey numbers, document locations, hearing date/venue and submission deadline. Check for postponements and corrigenda.
2. Obtain the available EIA, summary, maps and related application documents. Note the language and version used, and request access through the named authority if material is missing.
3. Use the [consultation submission](/guides/templates/17-environment-consultation.txt). Identify a specific impact, the page/map it concerns, local evidence and the answer or change sought.
4. Submit through the method in the notice, retain receipt, and request that written points be considered and recorded. If speaking at a hearing, bring a written copy.
5. Obtain the hearing proceedings, responses and eventual decision. Track conditions and compliance separately from the consultation.

Useful questions concern drainage/flooding, water demand, waste destination, noise, traffic, habitat, alternatives and monitoring. State which observations you can substantiate. A general objection becomes more useful when it identifies the record, impact and requested decision.

**Verification needed EP06:** confirm whether consultation is required for the actual project, the current EIA framework and exemptions, notice language, deadlines and how corrections are handled. Do not reuse an expired hearing notice or a draft-law consultation window.

## 7. Use community biodiversity knowledge carefully

Ask the local Biodiversity Management Committee (BMC) for its current contact, meeting process and People's Biodiversity Register (PBR) route. GSBB describes BMC conservation/documentation functions and PBRs as records of local resources, uses and traditional knowledge. [BMC guidance][EN17]; [PBR guidance][EN18]

Offer dated observations, photographs, habitat descriptions and a clear request to record or consider the issue. Ask how corrections and sensitive knowledge are handled. Obtain permission before sharing somebody else's traditional knowledge, and avoid publicly revealing vulnerable wildlife locations. A PBR entry can support documentation; it is not a substitute for a notification, permit or specialist enforcement decision.

**Verification needed EP07:** confirm the current committee, meeting and records-access process, and any access/benefit-sharing or research permission applying to collection or commercial use. This guide does not authorise collecting biological material.

## 8. Follow the decision and protect appeal time

Keep one case log with every authority, receipt, inspection, notice and decision. Use the [reporting guide](/read/guide-reporting) for follow-up and RTI records requests. Ask for a reasoned written outcome and check whether stated remedial work actually happened.

If irreversible damage is continuing, or you receive a permission/order you may need to challenge, seek prompt advice on the correct statutory appeal, tribunal or court route. The NGT Act distinguishes environmental disputes, relief and appeals; not every complaint belongs in the same proceeding. An ordinary grievance or pending RTI request should not be assumed to suspend a legal filing period. [NGT Act, sections 14–16][EN19]

**Verification needed EP08:** a practitioner must verify jurisdiction, standing, cause-of-action/communication dates, limitation, permitted extensions and the current filing procedure. The fresh India Code PDF download timed out. No universal appeal deadline or guarantee of a stop order is supplied.

## Worked example and templates

If trucks are filling a field beside a lake, record the field and lake separately, their locations and the activity. Ask TCP about section 17A; ask GSWA for the lake's final status and boundary; refer possible blocked drainage to the responsible water/local authority. Ask GSPCB to inspect if waste is being dumped. Attach the same factual evidence index to each relevant request, identify the issue each office should decide, and track their separate responses.

- [Site and protection checklist](/guides/templates/15-environment-site-check.md)
- [Records and inspection request](/guides/templates/16-environment-records-and-inspection.txt)
- [Consultation submission](/guides/templates/17-environment-consultation.txt)

title: Report a problem in Goa
heading: Report a civic or environmental problem in Goa
summary: Gather evidence, choose the authority, follow up a complaint and request official records.
markdown:
**Draft for Act for Goa. Source review: 22 October 2026.**

Use this guide to document a problem, choose an authority, submit a complaint and keep track of the response. It also explains how to request official records through the Right to Information Act. It covers Goa's village and municipal areas; the correct office depends on where the problem is and what it concerns.

**Draft status:** steps marked **Verification needed** require the checks listed in the [verification register](/read/guide-verification) before publication. Contact details below were checked against published sources, not tested by calling or submitting a case. These drafts do not determine whether a particular activity is unlawful.

## Start here

If someone is in immediate danger, move to safety and seek emergency assistance. Use Goa's official emergency directory for police, fire and ambulance assistance. An administrative complaint or RTI application is not an emergency response. [Official helplines][R1]

For other problems:

1. Record exactly what you observed and where.
2. Choose the responsible office using the table below.
3. Submit a short factual complaint with relevant evidence.
4. Keep proof of submission and a reference number.
5. Follow up using that same reference. Request records through RTI if you need documentary evidence of permissions or action taken.

These five steps are practical recommendations. They do not create a legal deadline or replace a prescribed application or appeal procedure.

## Choose where to report

| Problem | Starting point | What to ask for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Missed waste collection, a public drain or another local sanitation problem | The Village Panchayat or municipal council/Corporation responsible for the location. If responsibility is unclear, use the CM Helpline to seek routing. | Identify the responsible service, inspect the location and give a reference for corrective action. |
| Smoke, waste burning, sewage discharge, industrial pollution or noise | Goa State Pollution Control Board (GSPCB); also identify the local body or utility responsible for the underlying service. | Inspection, appropriate measurements or sampling, verification of relevant permissions, and action within the authority's powers. |
| Suspected unauthorised construction in a village | Village Panchayat, addressed to its Secretary/Sarpanch. Send planning questions to the relevant TCP office or PDA as well. | Check the licence, approved plans and conditions; inspect the reported work. |
| Suspected unauthorised construction in a town | The municipal council's Chief Officer or the Corporation's designated building authority; the planning authority for planning issues. | Check permission and inspect. Margao publishes a procedure involving inspection, notice, hearing and an order; other towns must confirm their own route. |
| Tree felling or damage to forest land | The Forest Department office responsible for the location; ask for the Range Forest Officer/Tree Officer or the appropriate forest authority. | Verify permissions and conditions and inspect the reported activity. |
| Hill cutting or filling low-lying land | TCP, asking for the office dealing with section 17A; notify the local body about associated construction. | Verify the applicable land classification and prior permission. |
| Coastal work, wetland filling or interference with a watercourse | The relevant environmental authority: GCZMA for coastal regulation; the Wetland Authority for notified-wetland questions; Water Resources for its water-management functions. Use the Environment Department or CM Helpline to establish the correct office if uncertain. | Identify the applicable protection, responsible authority and permissions, and arrange inspection where warranted. |
| Suspected animal cruelty | Local police and appropriate veterinary/Animal Husbandry assistance. Wildlife cases also require the Forest Department. | Record the complaint, arrange appropriate assessment and consider action under the applicable law. |

Basis: [Panchayat charter, printed pages 19–20][R2]; [Margao construction complaints][R3]; [GSPCB][R4]; [TCP section 17A procedure][R5]; [Environment Department charter][R6]; [Goa animal-cruelty SOP][R7]. The table is a starting-point guide, not an exclusive allocation of legal jurisdiction.

**Verification needed R03:** confirm the relevant forest range, coastal/wetland authority, utility and municipal office for the location. Complete the proposed locality directory before publishing specific office contacts. The 2020 animal-cruelty SOP is scanned and cites older criminal provisions. Its first page was visually checked; detailed offence and procedure instructions need a review against current law.

## Use these published complaint channels

**Pollution:** GSPCB's website says complaints and grievances are accepted at **mail.gspcb@gov.in**. It also publishes an [online complaint page][R8] and a source-listed noise helpline. Keep the sent email and attachments; ask for the complaint number. The online page requires JavaScript. These are source-listed channels; receipt, staffing and resolution have not been tested. [GSPCB announcement][R4]

**General government grievances:** the [CM Helpline portal][R9] publishes its current contact route and describes online/phone registration with a tracking ID. Give the location, department if known, facts, requested action and supporting documents. Save the ID and check its status. Ask which department received the case.

**Verification needed R01:** confirm the live submission flow, receipt process and current contact details. Different government pages list different general grievance numbers; use the CM Helpline portal to confirm its own published contact route. The portal's advertised resolution estimates are not used here as statutory deadlines.

For paper submission, take a copy and request an inward stamp, date and reference on your copy. If posting, retain the delivery evidence. Where an office prescribes its own form, complete that form and attach the factual statement from the template.

## Prepare the evidence

Create one folder for the case. Include:

- Location: village/town, ward, taluka, a landmark and a map pin. Add survey/subdivision numbers if known; mark uncertain identifiers as unconfirmed.
- Dates and times, including whether the problem is continuing or recurring.
- A short account separating what you saw from what somebody told you.
- Original photos or video with a simple index describing each file. Preserve originals; use copies for annotations.
- Relevant letters, permission numbers or public notices, if available.
- The action you seek: inspection, verification of permission, repair, collection, sampling, a written decision or another specific response.

Observe from somewhere you may lawfully be. Do not enter a worksite or private property to obtain evidence, confront workers, or handle suspected hazardous material. Describe uncertainty plainly: “I could not see a permission board from the public road” is more accurate than “there is no permission.”

For noise, note the source, location, time and duration. A phone recording can support an account; do not present it as an official calibrated noise measurement. For suspected pollution, record visible or sensory observations and request official assessment rather than declaring the substance's composition.

## Write and submit the complaint

Use the [complaint template](/guides/templates/01-complaint.txt). A useful subject is:

```text
Request for inspection of [observed issue] at [location], observed on [date]
```

State the facts, attach an indexed evidence list and request an acknowledgement, inspection where appropriate, and a written response. If a person or company is unidentified, say so. Do not guess a name or allege an offence you cannot substantiate.

Provide the contact information needed for a response. If disclosure could expose you to retaliation, ask how your details will be handled; do not assume an ordinary complaint will remain anonymous or confidential. Keep unnecessary identity documents out of public copies.

## Follow up and escalate

Record the office, submission date, reference, promised response date and what happened. Use the [case log](/guides/templates/05-case-log.md). If the office supplies no timeframe, ask for one and set your own reminder; label that as a personal follow-up date, not a statutory deadline.

Use the [follow-up template](/guides/templates/02-follow-up.txt) when the promised date passes, the problem continues, or a closure message does not address it. Refer to the original complaint and attach only relevant new evidence. Ask for the inspection/action record and the next responsible officer.

**Village construction complaints:** the Directorate's charter describes approaching the **Block Development Officer** when the Panchayat fails to act, followed by the **Deputy Director of Panchayats** where inaction continues. Sections 66(5)–(7) of the Panchayat Act address supervisory action and appeals. An administrative escalation and an appeal against an order are different procedures. [Charter, printed pages 19–20][R2]; [Panchayat Act, section 66][R10]

**Verification needed R04:** confirm the current office, statutory provision and any relevant order before giving a case-specific appeal deadline. The charter is historical guidance. Do not apply this village route to municipal cases, and do not wait for a grievance response if an appeal period is already running.

For an unresolved departmental service issue, check its grievance officer and whether the particular service is covered by Goa's notified time-bound service framework. That framework does not automatically give every environmental complaint the same deadline. Seek legal advice promptly for a notice, appeal or urgent court remedy; the [Goa legal-aid service][R11] explains eligibility and available assistance.

## Use RTI when you need official records

An RTI application asks a public authority for information it holds. It does not itself order a site inspection or stop construction. Indian citizens can use the Act. [RTI Act, sections 3 and 6][R12]

Ask for identifiable records and a defined period. Useful requests include:

- Copies of the planning permission, building licence, sanctioned plans and amendments for a specified property.
- Inspection reports, notices, recorded decisions and action-taken records concerning a numbered complaint.
- The applicable rule, circular, published fee schedule or officer-designation record.

Use the [RTI template](/guides/templates/03-rti-records-request.txt), addressed to the public authority's State Public Information Officer (SPIO). It asks for existing records, allows partial disclosure where appropriate and requests transfer of relevant parts if another public authority holds them. Exemptions and third-party procedures can affect disclosure; do not promise access to every record.

The [Goa RTI Online portal][R13] advertises application and appeal services. Its FAQ describes first appeals using the original registration number and email. **Verification needed R02:** direct retrieval of the portal failed during this review, so confirm the live authority list, upload limits, fee/payment route and paper alternative before publication. A portal outage does not remove the option of writing to the correct SPIO.

The Goa fee rules in the corpus specify a **₹10 application fee** and address further charges. Confirm the presently accepted payment method and any applicable copying/certification charge; keep the receipt. The Act provides a fee exemption for people below the poverty line, subject to the applicable proof requirements. [Goa fee rules, rule 3][R14]; [RTI Act, section 7(5)][R12]

## Keep RTI deadlines separate from complaint follow-up

| RTI stage | Statutory starting point |
| --- | --- |
| Ordinary SPIO response | Generally within 30 days of receipt. |
| Information concerning life or liberty | 48 hours; this concerns information, not emergency intervention. |
| Transfer to another public authority | As soon as practicable, within 5 days. |
| First appeal | Ordinarily within 30 days after the response deadline expires or the decision is received. |
| First-appeal decision | Normally 30 days; up to 45 with reasons recorded. |
| Second appeal | Ordinarily within 90 days of when the first-appeal decision should have been made or was received. |

Source: [RTI Act, sections 6(3), 7 and 19][R12]. Calculate the deadline for the actual case: APIO submission adds time, additional-fee notices can pause the response clock, and third-party procedures have separate provisions. Delayed appeals may be admitted for sufficient cause; do not depend on that discretion.

**Verification needed R05:** the time limits above were checked in the collected official Act text. Compare it with the latest consolidated Act before publication, especially the disclosure provisions; the newer India Code download was unavailable during this review.

If there is no timely response or the answer is incomplete, use the [first-appeal template](/guides/templates/04-rti-first-appeal.txt) and identify the exact unanswered items. Keep the original application, receipt, response and relevant dates. The portal FAQ says it charges no first-appeal fee; reconfirm the current route under R02. A second appeal requires its own current Commission procedure and is outside this template pack.

## A short worked example

You see soil being tipped into a low-lying area beside your village road. Record the location and dates from the public road. Describe the tipping and visible drainage obstruction; do not label the land a notified wetland without records. Ask TCP about section 17A and notify the local body about the drainage concern. Seek environmental-authority routing if protection may apply. Submit the complaint, preserve the receipt and use a separate RTI request for permissions and inspection records. Track the complaint and RTI on separate lines in the case log.

## Sources and review notes

The [source register](/read/guide-sources) provides local corpus copies, document sections and verification limits. The [verification register](/read/guide-verification) records R01–R05 and the remaining editorial checks. This guide adapts the useful approach of Act for Goa's [tree-reporting resource](https://actforgoa.org/resource/report-tree-cutting/) and [illegal-construction pamphlet](https://actforgoa.org/resource/illegal-construction-pamphlet/) while linking the procedures to official material.

title: Building and repair in Goa
heading: Plan building or repair work in Goa
summary: Check land and jurisdiction, organise permissions, and understand completion and occupancy.
markdown:
**Draft for Act for Goa. Source review: 22 October 2026.**

Use this guide before commissioning building work, an extension, reconstruction, a change of use or repairs. It helps you identify the land and responsible authorities, assemble the application, check what must happen before work starts, and obtain the required completion and occupancy documents.

This is the standard planning and local-licensing route. Special procedures and exemptions may apply. **Verification needed** notes identify unresolved legal or service details in the [verification register](/read/guide-verification). A particular plot's title, zoning, permissions and environmental restrictions require case-specific checking by the relevant authority and qualified professionals.

## The usual sequence

1. Identify the plot, proposed work and existing permissions.
2. Establish which planning authority and local body cover the site.
3. Check land use, title/tenure, conversion and environmental restrictions.
4. Obtain the applicable planning permission or technical clearance and other approvals at the required stages.
5. Obtain the local building licence or repair permission and satisfy its conditions before the relevant work.
6. Build to the sanctioned plans, give required stage notices and keep inspection records.
7. Obtain the applicable completion order and local occupancy certificate before occupation.

The planning and local-body stages are distinct in the [TCP procedure][B1]. The detailed requirements must be read with the [building regulations][B2], amendments and the conditions of each approval.

## Identify the work before choosing a form

Write a one-paragraph scope: what exists, what you want to change, the proposed use, approximate area and whether structural work, new floors, subdivision, excavation, filling or tree removal is involved. Photograph the existing condition and collect any approved plans and licences.

| Proposed work | First question to resolve |
| --- | --- |
| New building, reconstruction or extension | Which planning approval and local construction licence apply? |
| Repairs to an existing building | Does the proposed scope qualify as repairs, and what permission is required? |
| Change of use or subdivision | What separate planning, land-use and local permissions apply? |
| Hill cutting, filling or tree removal | What separate permission is required before that activity? |
| An existing building with missing or disputed permissions | What is its documented status, and what lawful route, if any, applies? |

**Verification needed B02:** do not label structural alteration or expansion as “repairs” yourself. Margao publishes a repair procedure involving ownership/survey documents, photographs, an engineer's stability certificate, inspection and permission. Its requirements are a local example, not a statewide checklist. The Panchayat charter also describes a limited repair route, but its current scope and conditions need confirmation. [Margao repair procedure][B3]; [Panchayat charter, printed pages 24–25][B4]

## Establish the two responsible authorities

Ask which planning area contains the site. A village address does not by itself establish TCP jurisdiction, and a municipal address does not by itself establish PDA jurisdiction.

| Planning jurisdiction | Standard planning stage | Local stage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| An area under a Planning and Development Authority (PDA) | Apply to that PDA for development permission. | Apply to the relevant Panchayat, municipal council or Corporation for the local licence/permit. |
| An area under TCP rather than a PDA | Apply to the responsible Town and Country Planning office for technical clearance. | Apply to the relevant Panchayat, municipal council or Corporation for the local licence/permit. |

This distinction comes from the [official TCP procedure][B1]. Ask for confirmation using the village/town, survey/subdivision number and location plan. Use the [project and permission enquiry template](/guides/templates/06-project-enquiry.txt) to record the answer.

**Verification needed B01:** confirm the current jurisdiction and plan applicable to the particular property. **B02:** the TCP downloads page also lists Notary Architect Engineer forms for certain single-family dwellings. The eligibility, current operation and conditions of that special route have not been verified; this guide does not assume it is available. [TCP forms][B5]

## Check the land before committing to the design

Build a property file with your registered professional and, for title or tenure questions, a lawyer experienced in Goa land matters.

| Check | Obtain or establish | Keep in the file |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exact parcel and access | Survey/subdivision or city-survey identifiers, survey plan, boundaries and documented access | Certified/current records and the plan used for the application |
| Right to carry out the work | Ownership or other legally sufficient interest; relevant succession, co-owner or authority documents | The instrument and advice establishing the applicant's authority |
| Applicable planning controls | Current zoning information, relevant Regional/Outline Development Plan, amendments and any site-specific orders | Official extracts and the authority's written response |
| Land conversion | Whether conversion is required, already granted, or subject to restrictions | Applicable conversion sanad and conditions, or written clarification of the route |
| Other restrictions | Agricultural tenure/transfer, comunidade or mundkar issues, forest status, coastal or wetland restrictions, heritage constraints and any court orders that affect the property | Relevant records, approvals and unresolved questions |

TCP's published document list includes survey and record-of-rights material, evidence of interest in the land, professional certificates and conversion documentation. These papers serve different purposes: ask the professionals to establish both the right to develop and the permitted development. [Technical-clearance procedure PDF][B6]; [Land Revenue Code and Rules][B7]

For agricultural land, obtain specific advice on the [2023 transfer restrictions][B8] and other applicable tenancy/land-use rules. Owning a property, holding a tax receipt or seeing a settlement colour on a map does not by itself demonstrate that the proposed building is permitted. Ask which documents establish each required element rather than treating one document as approval for everything.

**Verification needed B03:** the applicable zoning, conversion, tenure, environmental boundaries and any litigation are plot-specific. Do not use a draft map or draft wetland notification as evidence of final legal status. The corpus is a reference library, not a parcel-level clearance service.

## Screen for additional permissions

Tell the designer and authorities about these features at the start:

- **Coastal location:** establish the applicable coastal plan/classification and whether GCZMA approval is required. Use the official maps and site records, not a guessed distance from the water.
- **Trees or forest land:** check tree-felling/removal permission and any separate forest restriction. A building licence should not be assumed to authorise these activities.
- **Hill cutting or filling low-lying land:** TCP publishes a separate section 17A permission process and supporting-plan requirements. Raise this even if the work is described as levelling the plot. [Section 17A procedure][B9]
- **Wetlands, drains and watercourses:** establish the applicable protection and drainage requirements before changing ground levels or drainage.
- **Heritage/conservation, fire and other restrictions:** ask whether conservation review, fire clearance, airport/defence/railway permissions or other NOCs apply. [Building regulations][B2]

**Verification needed B03 and B04:** the applicability and sequence of these approvals depend on the site and project. An unresolved restriction is a question to settle before the affected work, not an item to defer until occupancy. No blanket setback, floor-area ratio, height, CRZ distance or exemption is stated here.

## Assemble and submit the application

Engage professionals registered and competent for the relevant work. Ask who will prepare the plans, take structural responsibility, supervise construction and certify completion. Registration and competence categories appear in the [TCP downloads][B5].

Use the [application and pre-work checklist](/guides/templates/07-building-checklist.md) to organise:

- The current application and questionnaire for the relevant authority.
- Land/title/authority documents and current survey/record material.
- Site, floor, elevation and section drawings, drainage/services details and structural material required for the proposal.
- Owner declarations and the applicable professional certificates.
- Conversion documents and relevant NOCs/approvals.
- The fee assessment and receipts.

This is a preparation list. The authority's current checklist determines the required set, format, certification and number of copies. [Technical-clearance procedure PDF][B6]

### Official forms to start from

| Stage | Published form or entry |
| --- | --- |
| PDA development permission | [Application under section 44][F1] |
| TCP technical clearance | Find the applicable TCP application and current procedure in [official downloads][B5]; confirm whether the current electronic route replaces the paper form. |
| Local village licence | [Village Panchayat building licence application][F2] |
| Municipal licence | [Municipal Council building licence application][F3]; a Corporation may require its own route. |
| Conversion recommendation | [Recommendation form][F4]; distinguish a planning recommendation from the conversion sanad issued under the revenue process. |
| Occupancy application | [Municipal Council/Village Panchayat application][F5] |

**Verification needed B05:** forms linked by an official site may still be older versions. Confirm the accepted form, current online/paper process, enclosures and copies with the receiving authority. TCP links to BPAMS; its submission process and current coverage were not tested. Use the TCP website to reach it rather than an unofficial intermediary. [TCP downloads][B5]

At each submission, retain the complete version submitted, acknowledgement, application number and payment receipt. If more information is requested, answer by reference to the same file and save the revised version. Ask which stage has been approved and which approvals remain outstanding.

## Check the approval before work starts

Read the permission and licence with the sanctioned plans. Use the pre-work checklist to confirm:

1. The applicant, survey number, site, approved use and plan version match your project.
2. The necessary planning permission/technical clearance and local licence are in place for the work being started.
3. Conditions that apply before that work, including conversion and conditional environmental/NOC requirements, have been satisfied.
4. The work falls within the approval's validity and scope; any renewal or amendment is dealt with.
5. The professional responsible for supervision knows the inspection and stage-notice requirements.

**Verification needed B04:** recent building-regulation amendments are in the corpus, including a TCP-hosted notification dated 6 August 2026. Their commencement, effect and any related court directions have not been fully consolidated. The designer must use the rules legally applicable to the project, not just the original 2010 document. [TCP regulations and amendments][B10]

**Verification needed B06:** fees, time limits, renewals and appeal rights vary by service and approval. Ask for the applicable notification and a written fee calculation. The Panchayat Act contains specific appeal/deeming provisions concerning permission applications; a receipt or elapsed time alone is not enough to establish that those conditions have been met. Get case-specific advice before relying on a deemed approval. [Panchayat Act, section 66][B11]

Regularisation of an existing unauthorised structure is a separate question. Do not treat the existence of a regularisation law or payment demand as advance permission for new work.

## Keep records during construction

Keep the sanctioned plans and approvals available to the supervising professional. Record stage notices, inspections, directions, revised approvals and dated site photographs. TCP publishes a stage-intimation form, while the Panchayat charter describes commencement, plinth and completion notices. Confirm the stages and submission method specified for your project. [TCP downloads][B5]; [Panchayat charter, printed page 24][B4]

Ask for the required approval before departing from the approved design or use. Record the authority's answer; do not assume a change can be settled at completion. Keep excavation, drainage, tree and waste conditions with the main site documents so the contractor can follow them.

**Verification needed B07:** confirm applicable construction-worker registration, cess, safety and waste obligations for the project. This draft does not calculate them. The corpus includes Goa construction-worker rules and newer construction-and-demolition waste rules; their application needs a separate project check. [Labour Department charter][B12]; [construction waste rules][B13]

## Complete the approval process before occupation

Plan the handover early. Under the ordinary process, the planning authority's completion order and the local body's occupancy certificate are distinct documents. A contractor's handover or a professional's completion certificate is not a substitute for both authority stages where they are required. [TCP procedure][B1]

Ask the supervising professional for the relevant completion certification, structural-stability certification and final/as-built drawings, including any approved revisions. Obtain the applicable planning completion order, then apply to the local body for occupancy and satisfy inspection and clearance requirements. Use the [completion and occupancy enquiry](/guides/templates/08-completion-enquiry.txt) to establish the accepted checklist. [Technical-clearance procedure PDF][B6]; [occupancy application][F5]

Keep the issued orders, approved final plans, certificates, conditions and receipts in the property file. Verify whether occupancy is full or partial and whether any conditions remain.

**Verification needed B08:** confirm the current completion/occupancy route for the authority, project category and any special approval scheme. Separate operating licences may be needed for business use; occupancy is not a universal licence to run a commercial activity.

## If you are checking somebody else's construction

Use the [reporting guide](/read/guide-reporting). Identify the parcel, record what is visible from a lawful location, request permissions and plans from the authorities, and describe suspected discrepancies factually. The absence of a visible notice board alone does not prove there is no permission. Ask the authority to inspect rather than making a definitive accusation yourself.

## Sources and review notes

The [source register](/read/guide-sources) links the official sources to saved corpus copies and exact sections/pages. The [verification register](/read/guide-verification) lists B01–B08 and the remaining review work. Act for Goa's existing [construction resources](https://actforgoa.org/resource/application-form-for-village-construction-licences/) and [illegal-construction pamphlet](https://actforgoa.org/resource/illegal-construction-pamphlet/) remain useful starting points; the official forms above avoid relying on inaccessible legacy-domain links.
